Read a level, and the region over which it is not distinguishable, off a profile

Source: R/resolution-profile.R
select_resolution.Rd

Picks the level a criterion prefers, together with the flat region: every level whose criterion value is within tol of the optimum. On the default profile, one size scored for pooled values, the default criterion is that size: it returns the count the size gives, with no optimum and no flat region (see "A profile built with an estimate"); what follows is about the criteria read on a ladder of counts. On the criteria this package computes the flat region is routinely wide: the reliability curve is flat to within 2 percent over a factor of 3–6 in the number of cells, and \(C_p\) on a smooth field descends to the support ceiling. The region is the answer, and the argmin only a point in it. When the optimum sits at an end of the levels the criterion was scored at, the result says so and names the bound, because a bound is then doing the choosing rather than the criterion (see resolution_profile for what each criterion measures and what it returns in practice). The functions that take the result as a cell count raise that as a warning of class spatialkit_bound_chosen.

Usage

select_resolution(
  profile,
  criterion = c("auto", "cp", "reliability", "elbow", "moran_z", "loo", "size"),
  tol = 0.02,
  range_floor = TRUE,
  diagnostic = FALSE,
  obs_per_cell = NULL
)

Arguments

profile

A resolution_profile.

criterion

Which rule sets the count: "cp" (minimised), "reliability" (maximised at or above the range floor), "elbow" (maximised), "loo" (the leave-one-out error of the profile's estimate, minimised), "size" (the count obs_per_cell gives), "auto" ("size" for a profile of pooled values, "loo" for one of plain means, "cp" for a profile without an estimate) or, with diagnostic = TRUE, "moran_z" (\(|z|\) minimised). Default "auto". "cp" was the default of earlier versions; name it to read \(C_p\) on a profile that has it.

tol

Width of the flat region. For cp, reliability and loo it is relative to the optimum's value (0.02 keeps levels within 2 percent of it); for elbow and moran_z, whose optimum can be zero, it is relative to the criterion's range over the ladder. Under "size" there is no flat region, and tol is the margin by which the cells have to beat one mean for structured and nothing else.

range_floor

For criterion = "reliability" only. TRUE (default) reads the criterion at the levels at or above the range floor in attr(profile, "bounds"), which is where resolution_profile() started the ladder by default up to version 2.0.0. It applies when the layer supports the floor, some scored level reaches it, and the profile built its own ladder (a ladder set with levels is read as given). FALSE reads every level.

diagnostic

criterion = "moran_z" is refused, with an error of class spatialkit_diagnostic_criterion that says what the column measures, unless this is TRUE: moran_z is a diagnostic of the cell means, not a count rule. Default FALSE.

obs_per_cell

For criterion = "size": the mean number of rows per cell wanted, a single number of at least 1 (fractions are allowed). NULL (default) is the profile's own size when it was built at exactly one (resolution_profile(obs_per_cell = )), and 4.5 otherwise. Given with a criterion that is not "size" it is an error.

Value

A list of class resolution_selection with best (the level), flat (the levels in the flat region, ascending; a set, which can skip a rung), criterion, value (the optimum), at_ceiling and at_floor (logical: the optimum is the last or first of the levels this criterion was read at, which for moran_z starts above nine cells and for reliability at the range floor; both NA under "size", which searches for no optimum), edge (which bound that is, in words: the support ceiling, the subsample's ceiling, the range floor, the ladder's own end, the finest or the coarsest size offered on a ladder obs_per_cell set, the only level scored, or the first or last level the criterion is computable at; NA for an interior optimum and under "size"), n_levels, values (the criterion at every level, NA where it could not be computed), structured (for cp: FALSE when cp at one cell is within tol of the optimum, when the cell means at the optimum differ from one mean by no more than chance allows, or when the variogram found no spatial structure; TRUE when the optimum beats one cell on both counts; see "What each criterion returns". For loo and size on a profile built with estimate: FALSE when the leave-one-out error of one mean for all scored rows is within tol of the error at best, or below it, or when the cell means at best differ from one mean by no more than chance allows; TRUE when the cells beat one mean on both counts. TRUE for an elbow; NA for reliability and moran_z, and for a profile that carries no one-cell value), one_cell (cp at one cell under cp; the leave-one-out error of one mean for all scored rows under loo and size; NA otherwise), structure_p (the p-value of the F test of the cells at best against one mean, multiplied by the number of levels searched and capped at 1; a size searches one level; NA where structured is not read off cp or the leave-one-out error), range_floor (the floor reliability was held to, or NA), note (what the flags mean, in words: a character vector, one note an element; NULL when there is nothing to say. The notes written under "loo" and "size", and for a profile built with estimate or with one size, carry names: size (the size that set the count), held (a size the profile held to the most cells k-means can place), structure (why the count is not identified), finest (the lowest error of pooled values is at the finest level scored), estimate (cp scores plain means, on a profile of pooled values) and ladder (the ladder is one size). A note of cp or moran_z about the criterion itself has no name. The warning of class spatialkit_no_structure that the functions taking the selection as a count raise carries every note but those named size, held, finest, estimate and ladder) and seeds (an sf POINT layer, with seed_id, of the centres of the partition the profile scored at best, in the CRS it was computed in; NULL for a profile that does not carry them). Their Voronoi cells are the cells that were scored; get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans", n = <this>) and voronoi_seeds_kmeans(k = <this>) return them. For a profile built with partition = "density" or init = "random" the list also has partition (kind, init, density_power, density_k), and the seeds carry it as attr(, "partition"); the regions are those the profile built, whatever kind built them.

For "loo" and "size", and for any criterion on a profile built with estimate, the list has these elements after seeds (partition, when there is one, stays last): estimate (the profile's, "mean" or "pooled"; NA for a profile without one); obs_per_cell (rows per cell at best: the rows a size divides over best; NA for an object that keeps no row count); obs_per_cell_asked (the size asked for; NA unless the criterion is "size"); scored_per_cell (the profile's column at best: the rows the leave-one-out error read over the cells that hold one. It is not obs_per_cell: it leaves out rows the error did not read and cells that hold none of them, as under select_on = "split"); loo and loo_one_cell (the leave-one-out error at best and that of one mean for all scored rows); share_alone and own_weight (the profile's columns at best); and count_rule, a list of class spatialkit_count_rule that records how the count was set: rule (the criterion applied), estimate (the estimate the rule was computed for: the profile's for "size" and "loo", "mean" for "cp", NA otherwise), cells, obs_per_cell, obs_per_cell_asked, response, n (the rows the size divides), n_points, n_fit (the rows the centres were fitted to; fewer than n_points for a subsample), seed, features, scored (what the profile scored at best for its estimate: estimate, n, cells, loo, loo_se, loo_one_cell, share_alone, own_weight, structured, rows and centres, the matrix of the centres the rows were scored in, in crs and in the profile's order; NULL without an estimate), partition, crs and scored_cells (NA: the record stands for a count). seeds carries the same record as attr(, "count_rule") with scored_cells = TRUE, since they are the centres that were scored. The record travels on with the seeds, the cells and the assigned layer to summarize_by_cell(), which warns when it reports another cell value than the count was chosen for (class spatialkit_estimate_mismatch) and when the cells or rows it is given are not the ones the count was scored on (spatialkit_cells_differ). Under "loo" and "size" one_cell holds the leave-one-out error of one mean and range_floor is NA. criterion is the criterion applied, never "auto".

What each criterion returns

cp

The level that minimises Mallows' \(C_p\): the count at which re-measuring the sampled sites, each predicted by its cell's mean, has the least estimated error (resolution_profile says what that leaves out for a new location). On a smooth response with little noise that is the support ceiling. The result also says whether the optimum beats one cell for the whole layer (attr(profile, "one_cell")), in structured. It is TRUE when two things hold: \(C_p\) at one cell is above the optimum by more than tol, and the cell means at the optimum differ from one mean by more than chance allows. The second is the F test of the cells against one mean, \((TSS - RSS) / (L - 1)\) over \(RSS / (m - L)\), at 5 percent after a Bonferroni adjustment for the levels the optimum was searched over (structure_p is the adjusted p-value). The cells are fitted to the coordinates alone, so the test holds its level on a response with no spatial structure whatever \(C_p\)'s noise variance is, and it is what decides when that variance is 0: \(C_p\) is then \(RSS / n\), which falls with every finer level by chance alone, and the first comparison says nothing. When either fails, structured is FALSE: one mean for the whole layer predicts as well as any level scored, so the response shows no spatial structure the cells can use and the count is not identified. structured is also FALSE when the profile's variogram was refused for showing no spatial structure. best is still the argmin. Measured on white noise (uniform points, the automatic ladder of obs_per_cell = NULL), structured was TRUE on 3 of 200 layers of 60 points, 7 of 200 of 120, 5 of 150 of 300 and none of 80 of 600 or of 40 of 1,500 with the noise variance taken from the finest level; and with the package's own variogram, whose nugget was 0 on 27 of the 180 layers, on none of 120 layers of 120 points and 3 of 60 of 300. The first comparison alone gave 27, 20, 8, 0 and 0, and then 38 and 11. The F distribution is exact for a Gaussian response, and the test held its level on others: with no structure in a lognormal response, a 0/1 response with mean 0.1 and a \(t_3\) response, structured was TRUE on 2 to 10 of 200 layers at each of 60, 120 and 300 points. A FALSE on a small layer is weak evidence that there is no structure: on exponential fields (range parameter 100 on a 1000-unit extent, nugget 0.3 on a unit sill) structured was TRUE on 12 of 40 layers of 60 points, 36 of 40 of 120 and 40 of 40 of 300.

reliability

The coarsest count the range allows. The reliability curve peaks below the range floor, so it is read at the levels at or above the floor the profile reports (when the layer supports the floor and the profile built its own ladder). The floor is a level of every such ladder, so the result is the floor, with edge naming it (on a profile whose k-means failed at that level, the first level above it). range_floor = FALSE reads every level and returns the curve's own maximum, which is usually a count below the floor.

elbow

The number of clusters of the points, when they cluster; an error otherwise, because the column is NA at every level unless the WSS curve bends.

moran_z

Refused unless diagnostic = TRUE. It is the level at which neighbouring cell means (or, with predictors, their regression residuals) are least autocorrelated. \(|z|\) is near 0 at 10 to 20 cells whatever the data and grows as cells get finer than the range, so its minimum is usually the first level it can be computed at, or one near it, and it says nothing about how well the cells represent the response.

loo

The level with the lowest leave-one-out error of the estimate the profile was built for (resolution_profile(estimate = )); of levels with the same error, the one with the fewest cells. The flat region is every level whose error is within tol of the lowest. The column needs no variogram. structured is read as for cp, with the leave-one-out error in place of \(C_p\): it is TRUE when the error of one mean for all scored rows is above the optimum by more than tol and the F test of the cells at the optimum against one mean, adjusted for the levels searched, has \(p < 0.05\); one_cell then holds the error of one mean. Under this criterion the count depends on the values of the response. When the profile's estimate is the pooled value and the lowest error is at the finest level scored, a note says that the end of the ladder chose the count. For pooled values the error tends to keep falling to the finest level: in the simulation described under "Observations per cell" in resolution_profile, the lowest error of the pooled value was at the finest of seven sizes on 176 of 200 layers, and that of the plain mean on none. On a ladder obs_per_cell set, an optimum at an end has the edge "the finest size offered (obs_per_cell)" or "the coarsest size offered (obs_per_cell)"; a finest level the profile held to the most cells k-means can place keeps the label of the support ceiling.

size

The count a size gives, max(2, round(n / obs_per_cell)), with n the rows the size divides: the rows with a response, or every point for a profile without one. No optimum is searched for. The level returned is the first of three that applies: the level the profile built for that size; the count itself, when the profile has a partition at it; otherwise the built level nearest to the count on the log scale (of two as near, the one with fewer cells), with a warning of class spatialkit_size_not_reached, which says so when the count is more than k-means can place on the layer. It reads any profile, one built without a response or without an estimate included, but not a column subset, which has lost the row count. flat is the level, value the rows per cell it leaves (n / best), and at_ceiling, at_floor and edge are NA: no bound chose anything, so the functions that take the selection as a count raise no spatialkit_bound_chosen. Under this rule neither the cells, which are fitted to the coordinates, nor their number, which is a count of rows, depend on the values of the response. A size does not ask whether the response has structure the cells can use, so structured asks it separately, on a profile built with an estimate. It is FALSE when the leave-one-out error of one mean for all scored rows is within tol of the error at the level, or below it, or when the F test of the cells at the level against one mean has \(p \ge 0.05\). The count stands either way, since the caller set it: structured = FALSE says that the cell values will say little that one mean for the layer does not. The functions that take the selection as a count then raise spatialkit_no_structure. On a profile without an estimate structured is NA.

auto

The rule that goes with the profile's estimate: "size" for a profile built with estimate = "pooled", "loo" for estimate = "mean", and "cp" for a profile without an estimate. A column subset of a profile has lost the record of its estimate and is read by "cp". criterion in the result is the criterion applied, never "auto".

A profile built with an estimate

This function's default criterion is "auto": "size" for a profile of pooled values, "loo" for one of plain means and "cp" for a profile without an estimate. A profile built with estimate that is passed straight to get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans() or build_tessellation() as the count is read the same way, so select_resolution(profile) and the profile itself give the same count. A profile of pooled values built with a ladder argument (n_levels and the others) is read by the size as well: the default returns the level nearest the count the size gives, on the automatic ladder its top level, with spatialkit_size_not_reached. The default was "cp" in earlier versions, whatever the profile; criterion = "cp" reads it as before on a profile that has it. cp is computed on such a profile as on any other and scores plain means; when the profile's estimate is the pooled value the result's note says so.

"cp" and "reliability" cannot be read off a profile whose ladder obs_per_cell set under sac = "auto". Such a profile fits no variogram, both columns are NA at every level, and the call is an error that names the ways to get them: build the profile with sac = NULL, with a sac of your own, or with obs_per_cell = NULL. The default profile is such a profile. For the count "cp" gave in earlier versions, build the profile with estimate = NULL, obs_per_cell = NULL, and with partition = "kmeans" for the same regions. On a ladder of one size that has a variogram either criterion returns the one level, with edge "the only level scored".

For a ladder of one size, summary() of the profile lists each criterion that is finite at the level and says that the size set the count, and plot() draws each as one point, with no selected level and no band. When none is finite, as on a constant response, where loo is NA too, summary() stops with an error that says so.

See also

Other aggregation: assign_features_to_polygons(), cell_values_at(), determine_optimal_levels(), kriging_adequacy(), resolution_profile(), summarize_by_cell(), summary.resolution_profile()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("gstat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(sf)
  # An exponential field with range parameter 200 (true effective range
  # 600 m) on a 1 km square, with a nugget of 0.6 on a unit sill.
  set.seed(4)
  n <- 400
  xy <- data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000))
  D  <- as.matrix(dist(xy))
  xy$z <- as.numeric(t(chol(exp(-D / 200) + diag(0.6, n))) %*% rnorm(n))
  pts <- st_as_sf(xy, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)
  prof <- resolution_profile(pts, response_var = "z", n_levels = 12)

  sel <- select_resolution(prof, criterion = "cp")
  print(sel)               # the level, and the flat region around it
  print(sel$flat)          # every level within `tol` of the optimum
  print(sel$edge)          # the bound the optimum sits on; NA when interior
  print(sel$structured)    # FALSE when one cell for the layer does as well

  # Reliability prefers coarse cells: it is read at or above the floor the
  # autocorrelation range sets, and the result says in words that the
  # floor is choosing.
  rel <- select_resolution(prof, criterion = "reliability")
  print(rel)
  print(c(at_floor = rel$at_floor, edge = rel$edge))

  # The default profile is one size scored for pooled values, and the
  # default criterion, "auto", reads it by that size.
  select_resolution(resolution_profile(pts, response_var = "z"))
}
#> Resolution by cp: 44 cells
#>   flat region : 44 (1 of 12 levels)
#>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours)
#>   note        : the optimum is the support ceiling (n / min_cell_n); the
#>                 bound is choosing, not the criterion. Lower min_cell_n to see
#>                 whether the criterion keeps going.
#>   note        : cp scores plain means, and this profile's estimate is the
#>                 pooled value; criterion = "size" is the rule for it.
#> [1] 44
#> [1] "the support ceiling (n / min_cell_n)"
#> [1] TRUE
#> Resolution by reliability: 4 cells
#>   flat region : 4 to 6 (3 of 12 levels)
#>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours)
#>   note        : the optimum is the range floor (area / range^2); the bound is
#>                 choosing, not the criterion. Fewer cells would be wider than
#>                 the range and average over more than one patch of the field.
#>                           at_floor                               edge 
#>                             "TRUE" "the range floor (area / range^2)" 
#> Resolution by size: 89 cells
#>   size        : 4.5 rows per cell asked (obs_per_cell); 400 rows / 89 cells = 4.49
#>   cells       : density-weighted k-means++ starts (power 1, 8 neighbours)
#>   estimate    : pooled toward the 8 nearest cells
#>   at this size: 0.5% of the rows are alone in their cell; median own weight 0.45
#>   loo         : 0.896 (one cell for the layer: 1.23)
#>   note        : the count is set by obs_per_cell = 4.5, the caller's choice;
#>                 no criterion chose it.
